verdicts.reason: Compute_taint confirms Rs 10,754.44 of traced victim money remains in the account (tainted share 0.061%). The lien freezes only that amount out of a ~Rs 17.6 M balance, so the customer's own funds are untouched; even a likely-genuine account can hold stolen money received in good faith.

Signals strongly support the mule label: high pass-through (6.34), young account (162 days), 10 device-sharing and 15 phone-sharing links, and four prior mule labels across separate investigations. The lien of Rs 2,901.14 matches computed taint and is a negligible fraction of the ~Rs 92.8 M balance, posing no risk of freezing the customer's own funds.

An extreme pass-through ratio of 55.7 with only 2 payers and a prior mule label clearly supports the mule classification; nearly all tainted inflow (Rs 1,183.44 of Rs 1,183.44) was forwarded, leaving just Rs 0.32 of traced victim money.
